flagship.headline: Jack Paar shows American viewers a Beatles clip
flagship.summary_line_1: The Jack Paar Program showed a film clip of the Beatles performing She Loves You on January 3, 1964, per the Paul McCartney Project and Songfacts.
flagship.summary_line_2: It aired about five weeks before the band's live debut on The Ed Sullivan Show on February 9, and the clip below is the single from the band's Topic channel.

events.headline: The Beatles spend day two of the Get Back sessions at Twickenham
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles rehearsed at Twickenham Film Studios on January 3, 1969, the second day of the Get Back sessions, bringing Don't Let Me Down close to its final arrangement and working on I've Got a Feeling and Two of Us, per the Paul McCartney Project.
events.summary_line_2: Paul McCartney also introduced Maxwell's Silver Hammer that day, and the clip below is I've Got a Feeling from the band's Topic channel.

events.headline: Carl Wilson fails to report for Army induction
events.summary_line_1: Beach Boys guitarist Carl Wilson did not report for military service on January 3, 1967, after receiving his draft notice, and refused to comply on religious grounds, according to American Songwriter.
events.summary_line_2: A federal grand jury indicted him that April, and the clip below is God Only Knows, the Beach Boys song he sings lead on, from the band's official VEVO channel.

events.headline: Jack Paar shows American viewers a Beatles clip
events.summary_line_1: The Jack Paar Program showed a film clip of the Beatles performing She Loves You on January 3, 1964, per the Paul McCartney Project and Songfacts.
events.summary_line_2: It aired about five weeks before the band's live debut on The Ed Sullivan Show on February 9, and the clip below is the single from the band's Topic channel.

events.headline: The Beatles play the Astoria Theatre for the ninth night
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles played the Astoria Theatre in Finsbury Park, London, on January 3, 1964, the ninth concert there and part of The Beatles Christmas Show, per the Paul McCartney Project.
events.summary_line_2: Their setlist included I Want to Hold Your Hand, and the clip below is that single from the band's Topic channel.

events.headline: The Rolling Stones cut Route 66 and Carol at Regent Sound
events.summary_line_1: The Rolling Stones began recording their debut album at Regent Sound Studios in London on January 3, 1964, cutting Carol, Mona, Route 66, Walking the Dog and You Can Make It If You Try, according to Rolling Stones Data.
events.summary_line_2: The album was recorded between January 3 and February 25 and released that April, and the clip below is Route 66 from the band's Topic channel.

events.headline: The Beatles open a Scottish tour in Elgin
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles played the Two Red Shoes ballroom in Elgin on January 3, 1963, the first date of their Winter 1963 Scotland tour, which went on to Dingwall and Bridge of Allan, per the Paul McCartney Project.
events.summary_line_2: Their single Please Please Me followed on January 11, and the clip below is that song from the band's Topic channel.

events.headline: The Montgomery Brothers record Groove Yard
events.summary_line_1: Wes Montgomery, his brothers Buddy and Monk, and drummer Bobby Thomas recorded the Riverside album Groove Yard at Plaza Sound Studios in New York on January 3, 1961, per the Riverside Records discography at Jazzdisco.
events.summary_line_2: The session also produced Delirium and Doujie, and the clip below is the title track from the group's Topic channel.

events.headline: The Billy Taylor Trio records Interlude at Van Gelder Studio
events.summary_line_1: Pianist Billy Taylor, bassist Doug Watkins and drummer Ray Mosca recorded nine tracks, opening with You Tempt Me, at Van Gelder Studio in Englewood Cliffs, New Jersey, on January 3, 1961, for the album Interlude on Moodsville, per the Van Gelder Studio discography at Jazzdisco.
events.summary_line_2: The album was later reissued as Warming Up!, and the clip below is You Tempt Me from the trio's Topic channel, a track for fans of jazz and easy listening.

events.headline: Bobby Darin and Connie Francis duet on The Ed Sullivan Show
events.summary_line_1: Bobby Darin and Connie Francis shared the bill on The Ed Sullivan Show on January 3, 1960, and sang You Make Me Feel So Young and You're the Top together, per TheTVDB.
events.summary_line_2: It was the first Sullivan broadcast of the new decade, and the clip below is the duet from the show's official channel.
